# Chapter Nineteen: War (The Siege of Silvan)

WAR

Marcus looked out from the balcony of General Durass’s residence, from here he could see the fires from the camp of the Empress’s soldiers. “They have pushed into the territory, soon they will come for the city” he said hate dripping from every word the General came to join him “They will go no further, the rotary cannons stopped them cold” he answered, though speaking fact Marcus could hear the cold pleasure in the man’s voice.

He had watched as they had setup the trap and then the effect as they unleashed the power of the rotary cannons on the enemy. Upon viewing the collection of weapons, Marcus could see they still had a long way to go before they would reach the technology level he had left, but the resin, repeating rifles and rotary cannons were a hell of a start he thought.

The Silvan’s had grown and created a crystal slug creating something that even in his time was not yet freely available rounds that didn’t require a shell to fire, they had discovered the ability to grow slugs that were two different crystal hybrids and by piercing them both, created an explosion sending the majority of the shell out towards the enemy with the power of a magnum round.

He had carefully examined the weapons, the smooth bores told of the path they still had yet to travel, but the deviation from his own technological timeline spoke of some powerful weapons he reflected. “General, I have to ask I thank your people for helping those of the lowlands, but you mentioned something about other races” Marcus queried, the way the General had used the term bothered him. He had seen the changes done to these people, genetics altered with the use of science and magic had created something akin to a new race, one closer with the forest he thought.

The General studied the trees as Silvans leapt from branch to branch, staying behind trunks in an effort to spy on the camp at the bottom of the hill. He was quiet for a long time as Marcus regarded the large oval eyes and then he turned to face the Mage “There are others, changed by the first ones who live further to the north, however they keep to themselves, we stopped trying to talk to them ages ago, our people live on the border and even our interaction with those of the low lands have been limited. “People fear what they do not understand Master Mage, you will do well to remember that” he said his eyes hovering to the open collar of Marcus’s shirt where the blue pulsing runes were visible. He self consciously closed the jacket buttoning it up to his neck and turned back to the forest. “Whats next General?” Marcus asked and the other man’s face spread back into a predatory smile. “Well Master Mage, the enemy will meet our battle riders” he said and the young Mage cocked his head “I didn’t think you owned horses” he said and Durass chuckled “We don’t Master Mage, we don’t” he said turning and walking into the house, Leaving Marcus to stand alone on the porch. Looking down at the camp his hand unconsciously went to his waist and rested loosely on the curved blade attached there, the runes glimmering off the silver blade as sunlight played down the metal. The voices in his head were quiet, they had been for a while but the knowledge was still there, but the same way your body would get used to a foreign object in it his mind had adapted to the knowledge, he could access it, but it no longer overwhelmed him he thought still staring at the fires in the distance.

Even with the vast amount of knowledge in his mind he still didn’t know how to defeat the Empress’s guard and the Seers with there creatures, they would come, and he would fight but Marcus did not know if it would be enough. He knew there had been two Seer’s in the came, had sensed them and now more had come, along with more of the creatures they commanded, reaching out with his mind he closed his eyes, allowing his will to play over the forest as he felt ten seer’s and over eighty of the creatures in the came.

They had called everything here, pulled the Seers and creatures from the towns he reflected to fight here. What was so damn important that the Empress would need to ensure overwhelming force. Then he remembered the Black runes across Rogan’s body, his black eyes and the comments from the Ancient Sylvan mage, she had done it wrong. Did the Empress need to find the proper mixture or find the process for ensuring that adapting the runic magic to a mage worked properly? He thought about it, what was the consequences for not doing it correctly he wondered, and no answer came as it so often did these days. The knowledge he possessed didn’t have that answer he marveled.

He felt like a man out of time, his love was gone, his friend might even now be dead. Dara had left and Patrice was busy with the wounded, that was all he had in the world he thought a few friends and the memory of someone he loved more then life itself. Marcus knew he would fight; knew he would defend this strange race of people as his mind wandered over the memories of children playing and young couples lounging in the park. These people did not deserve the fate that came for them, but that wasn’t why Marcus would fight, that is not why tomorrow morning he would descend the elevator and put himself between the enemy and this city. It was simply because it was the Empress’s people who had take Orah from him, she did not deserve to win, did not deserve to succeed he thought turning from the forest and entering the house.

That night he dreamt of Orah, of the Empress and the darkness a darkness that called from beyond the sea, something is coming the shadowy visage of the Empress said as she stood among the black rocks of the beach and pointed out towards the ocean. A low thrum echoed from the ocean’s horizon, sounding a little closer each time it sounded. Orah’s arm snaked over his as his love leaned in close “Its evil Marcus, it is death that comes across the ocean” she said. Turning he looked into the eyes of the woman who had been his world. “Orah, Im sorry, I couldn’t save you” he whispered, smiling she opened her mouth to speak and to Marcus’s horror flame erupted, setting her on fire “Save them Marcus, watch the oceans, it comes for the power” her voice whispered as fire engulfed her.

He sat bold upright in bed and for a moment he searched the room for the flaming body of Orah realizing he was in the General’s guest room. A sound was echoing from the window, then reality descended onto him as he shot out of bed, He had no idea how long the alarm had been going off, but it couldn’t be good he thought. Throwing on his clothes, he grabbed the weapons and bolted from the room. The General was in the main foyer preparing to leave when he turned to see the Mage rushing down the stairs. Marcus could see the worried look on his face “They are marching up the hill, more of the Seers and creatures are present and they used kinetic force to destroy the rotary cannons.” He said turning to the door with Marcus on his heels. “We have one more line of defense before we have to retreat to the city itself and prepare for a siege” the General said.

Marcus stopped him putting a hand on the man’s shoulders “General, if they take the land before the city needs to be abandoned, the mages will throw fire until this entire city is engulfed, I think I know what they want and the condition of the city doesn’t matter” he said the General looked at the Mage and Marcus could see the stubborn determination in his eyes “We will not give up the city mage” he said turning and brushing Marcus’s hand off his shoulder. They rode the elevator down in silence both lost in thought of the coming battle. As it reached the bottom Durass stepped out and took a long silver horn from one of his soldiers. “You are going to want to see this Master Mage” he simply said and smiled as he raised the horn and blew a long note that resounded through the area, echoing off the trees.

All was quiet for a moment and then a cacophony of growls erupted from the other side of the field and everyone turned. Marcus’s jaw dropped as Silvan warriors erupted from the bushes on white Bengal tigers the size of small cars. The creatures were massive the riders looking almost tiny on the massive creatures. Saddles and reigns had been strapped onto them and they bounded across the large field, more growls erupting from the beasts. Marcus noticed the belts wrapped around the riders and couldn’t understand why they were tied into the saddle until the first of the creatures leapt against a tree and began to climb into the branches above. “That’s amazing” he breathed watching as it reached a large branch, bounded over it and launched itself into another tree and then another, finally directly above the army, the beast dropped into the battle. Twenty of the cats descended into the middle of the enemy and began to tear apart soldier after soldier. He had never seen anything like it.

Leaning forward he watched as the cats dominated the field as the riders pulled long curved swords, what the cats couldn’t get the riders did as bone and steel lashed out spilling blood and bone over the forest floor. For a moment Marcus hoped that they would win, that these animals and the surprise attack would win the day, but these soldiers were not inexperienced, they were well trained and battle hardened, and quickly moved into a defensive position locking in the animals as they held them off with spears and swords.

Marcus felt it before he saw it as the ten robed seers walked into the crowd of soldiers, moving them with power as they walked in a line towards the trapped animals. Some of the large cats had managed to leap over the soldiers retreating further up the hill, but eight of them still stood there ground, hissing, growing and slapping at the long steel tipped spears. The animals kept trying to move forward, angered by the weapons and then the Seers stood there, like the horsemen of the apocalypse, a line of black robed monks with the cowls raised showing only a shadow where their faces should be. Marcus’s eyes widened “get them out of there Durass” he said but it was too late, three of the Seer’s extended out hands and Marcus felt as the power roiled through them three of the animals exploding into flame as beast and man screamed and thrashed. “NO” Marcus screamed and with and thrust kinetic energy at his feet he launched into the air and sailed over the crowd of soldiers as they stood shocked at the sight of the engulfed and screaming animals. Sailing over the crowd, he pushed out with his power steadying his body as he arced in the air, the power in his runes running like water over his body as he came careening down towards the ground he pushed out once again with kinetic force, slowing himself and landing lightly on his feet. Now he stood before the Ten Chosen of the Empress another had pulled power and launched it towards another rider and his beast. Marcus flicked his hand in a well practiced motion that came from within the repository of knowledge in his mind and the energy ricocheted and a tree burst into flames nearby. “That’s enough” he said standing stalwart between the chosen and the Silvan’s.

There would be no more death he vowed looking over the black robed Lords of the Empress’s court. “This is finished Mages, there will be no more death upon this field unless its yours” he stated, his voice even as he delivered the threat. Eyeing the line, he fought back the nagging fear that whispered in the back of his mind. What the hell was I thinking he chastised himself, he knew he could beat one, he had fought Rogan, knew what he was capable of, but ten of them. Marcus didn’t know if he had the power to fight all of them.

The soldiers surrounding the group had gone quiet as the fighting stopped, everyone now focusing on the group of Mages standing in the center of the field facing each other. A laugh floated from the line and one stepped forward pulling back his cowl as Marcus recognized the face of Rogan, his obsidian eyes seemed to light with enjoyment as he took a few more steps and then stopping regarded Marcus as he shook his head. “We have been here before Marcus, but I didn’t expect you would be so willing to walk into my clutches after last time, but it seems as if you wish to be delivered to my Empress after all” he said shaking his head. Marcus took a breath anger overtaking the nagging fear as he watched the self righteous asshole strut like a peacock up and down the line. “This stops here Rogan, how many have you killed, how many have you destroyed in the name of power” Marcus shot accusingly at the other man.

Rogan stopped cocking his head and looking at Marcus “You defend these” he said waiving a hand at the soldiers surrounding him. “They are mundanes, they are meant to serve us Marcus, we are the powerful, the chosen. The Empress has a plan and the Mages will save the world, we will unite all people under our power and lead them to salvation. Surely you understand this” he said almost astonished that the other man would place himself in the same sentence with those who weren’t mages.

But Marcus didn’t like bullies, he liked entitled pricks less “That’s your problem Rogan, you actually think your better then them, you think for some reason that because you have a gift, instead of using it to benefit those around you, you instead think you should control them” Marcus observed and Rogan again looked confused “Of course we are, we are the strong, they are the weak. It is the natural order” he said as if the reason were self evident. Marcus shook his head and laughed but there was no humor in the sound “How many people have you killed to fuel your grab for power Rogan, you think your original, you really think you are the first people to do this, to rationalize this. Hell Rogan, its so common it’s a fucking cliché” he spat. “You make me sick, so here is the deal, surrender and I will let you live” Marcus stated.

For a moment the field was quiet, no one moved as everyone looked on in amazement as the small group continued to face off. Then Rogan threw his head back and laughed, Marcus could hear chuckles from the other Seer’s as well. Hell at least he was entertaining he thought, his stomach sinking as he realized, he was going to have to fight these men. Marcus did not think he would live, but maybe, just maybe he could hold them off long enough for Durass to come up with a plan to save the city, when he lost, they would turn their attention to those above him and the city would burn.

A vision of Orah, burning in bed as he burst into the room shot through his head and the anger overtook all fear pushing it out, leaving only the cold fire of vengeance heating his soul. With a resigned sigh he reached down, pulling the small black staff from his side and holding it loosely he began to pour power into the object, feeling the runes along the hilt heat in response.

If he was going to die, he would take as many as he could with him he thought tensing as he felt the power coursing through his runes and over his body as, for the first time in centuries a Runic Mage prepared for battle. The benefit of being able to see the flow of power became evident a moment later as he watched the two Mages on either end change as their runes began to glow power gathering and doubling as they pulled power to them. Without warning hands shot out and kinetic force flew from either side trying to catch Marcus off guard. But he had been prepared and with a flip of his wrist the staff extended, and he pulled it up flipping it over his hand and catching the kinetic strikes with the runes on the hilt. The energy absorbed by the staff.

Catching the staff as it finished its rotation, he pushed out his other hand and extended the staff towards the mage on the left, releasing the energy along with some of his own. He watched as the bolt of kinetic force slammed into the man, catching him in the chest and throwing him back into a line of trees. Cracking sounds erupted from his body as he hit the tree and what sounded like a wet smack resounded as his body hit the ground. The mage did not stand and for a moment no one said anything everyone frozen still, still looking to where the Mage, one of the Empress’s chosen had just been killed.

Rogan turned his head locking his eyes on Marcus and he could see the anger behind those black eyes as the man’s face twisted in rage “You will pay for that Mage” he spit. Rogan whistled and the nine remaining mages pulled their own staves, some splitting them revealing the dual blades, others extending it like a wand, the entire group’s weapons now trained on Marcus as he stood there waiting for the attack that would end his life. Rogan moved first as Marcus watched the mage collect energy, he pushed kinetic force into the ground below him, launching himself into the air, he split the small stave in two, flipping it so the hilt ends pointed at Marcus. As he reached the pinnacle of his arch gouts of flame shot from the end of the staves Marcus knocking it away without even a thought, he prepared for the mage to land. As Rogan’s feat touched the ground, Marcus collapsed his own stave, splitting it and holding it out daggers first.

Rogan rushed forward, throwing hit after hit and then a jet of flame and then a kinetic strike, the sticks moved with such speed, enhanced by his magic as he struck again and again but Marcus had the muscle memory and training of generations of mages and matched him blow for blow, knocking back strikes and parry magic the two stood there facing off as the hilts and blades clashed against each other, magic spitting off the weapons in arcs of flame and electricity. As he matched Rogan’s strikes, he felt the energy behind him as three of the Seers threw bolts of electricity at him. Marcus without even a thought threw down a kinetic blast careening him left and out of the way of the blasts. Rogan did the same the two mages crashing into a surprised group of soldiers who until that moment had been stunned, watching the two.

Rogan drew power, picking up Soldiers and throwing them at Marcus who quickly batted them out of the way, he moved towards his opponent. Rogan began to circle him, and Marcus responded, keeping the mage in front of him and then he stopped smiling “You have gotten stronger” he said and Marcus was about to respond when he felt the force of the remaining seers wrap around him., Kinetic energy snaking around his body like snakes as the energy tightened. Rogan still smiling relaxed his stance. “Oh, I don’t want you dead Marcus, our Empress has plans for you” he said standing there as energy continued to wrap Marcus into a kinetic cacoon.

No, he thought, he couldn’t let this happen. He wouldn’t allow the Empress to get ahold of him, he had no idea what she had planned but he knew it wouldn’t be good. Rogan turned his back on the young mage and looked up at the city as he conjured a small gout of flame in his palm as he continued to look up. Marcus looked to the flame, the memory of Orah still hung in his mind “No” Marcus whispered the power holding him in place, crushing the air out of him, he could no longer breath as blackness began to edge into his vision. “no” he said again as the Runic Mage began to gather power, the runes pulsing as he pulled more and more energy into himself. Closing his eyes he felt the kinetic vines of power seeing the power course over him, poking at the snakes of power his eyes snapped open as he felt the hollow centers of the spell and as a predatory smile spread across his face he launched all the accumulated energy into the vines of power breaking in through the outer shell his power shot back like water in a pipe and all at once the eight Mages were thrown off there feat and launched backward as the power exploded into them. The vines of power disintegrated, and Marcus was suddenly free. He had no time to pull more power, Rogan had started to turn so Marcus pushed the end of one of the staves towards him, expending the stored power within it, the Mage caught by surprise was thrown forward into a tree.

No more he thought turning to face the eight mages, one no longer moving the other seven stood shakily. Marcus stalked forward “No More” he yelled, pulling power as he felt the runes heating his skin as he continued to expend his gift. He thrust the blades towards two of the Black Robed figures as lances of fire shot into them, the two seers erupting into fire, no time to defend themselves and then flicking his finger he threw another kinetic strike at the next Seer, he quickly batted it away, but that had been a distraction as he threw one of the blades at the mage, putting magical force behind it, it sped like a bullet impaling the mage into the tree behind him.

He saw the kinetic blast as the next seer summoned it and before he could throw it, Marcus summoned electricity and lighting erupted from his fingers playing over the mage just as he began to try and throw the strike. He stood for a moment his body jerking as the electricity struck him over and over, finally Marcus let go, the Mages body falling to the ground. At that moment Marcus finally understood what it meant to be a Runic Mage, he no longer had to pull energy, no longer had to stop and recharge, he felt the energy coursing over his body, using the runes like a canal his runes pulling energy itself allowing him to keep throwing spell after spell the power coursing from his fingers was almost godlike he thought as he reached up pulling one of the larges trees out of the ground with magical force and slamming it on top of the remaining Seers.

He slowly turned to face a now unsteady Rogan, standing there with blood trickling down his face the Seer stood his ground. “I am the Empress’s chosen; I am all powerful, you will not best me Mage” he spat as Marcus regarded him silently. Reaching back with his hand Marcus summoned the staff blade and it came flying to his hand, he reassembled the small weapon, his eyes still not leaving Rogan’s. “Surrender” Marcus stepping towards the Empress’s chosen. Rogan smiled and then his hand moved in a blur throwing lightning of his own before marcus could react it hit his chest and was absorbed by his runes. Both men stood there astounded “What are you?” Rogan breathed his eyes wide now as he stared at the other man. “Your executioner” he said and with a wave of his shot a pillar of fire at the other Mage, the flame so hot the Mage’s scream only lasted for a moment before his body began to disintegrate.

“Surrender or Die” Marcus yelled to the field as the soldiers stood there astounded. Marcus now saw the Screamers retreating in the distance, they never even came to the Seer’s aid he thought shaking his head. Soldiers began to lay down their weapons and put their hands up as Wardens and Silvan’s secured prisoners as the battle for the city in the trees ended.
